title: The sunnah acts of Salah
intro: What the Prophet (SAW) did in Salah and taught us to do – they make Salah more complete.

learn.html: Believers should do the sunnah acts of Salah, because the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) did them and asked us to do them. If we leave one out, we do not have to repeat the Salah.

items: at the opening takbir, men raise their hands to their ears and women to their shoulders
in qiyam, folding the hands – men below the navel, right hand over left, holding the left wrist with thumb and little finger; women on the chest, right hand on the left
in qiyam, standing with the feet a hand’s width apart
reciting Subhanaka and A‘udhu billah in the first rak‘ah
reciting Bismillah before Al-Fatiha in every rak‘ah
saying Ameen quietly after Al-Fatiha
in ruku‘, holding the knees with the fingers
saying Sami‘allaahu liman hamidah and Rabbanaa lakal-hamd
saying the takbir when moving from one part of Salah to the next
saying Subhaana Rabbiyal-‘Azeem in ruku‘ and Subhaana Rabbiyal-A‘laa in sajdah
going down to sajdah: first the knees, then the palms, then the face – and the reverse when getting up
in sajdah, putting the forehead and nose down, fingers together and pointing to the Qiblah
men sitting on the left foot with the right foot upright, toes toward the Qiblah; women with both feet to the right side
putting the hands on the thighs or knees in the sitting between the two sajdahs
in sajdah, men keeping the stomach away from the knees and the elbows away from the body; women keeping them close
in the last sitting, and in the first sitting of the sunnah of Asr and Isha, reciting the salawat and duas after At-Tahiyyat
raising the right index finger at the Shahadah in At-Tahiyyat
giving the salam first to the right, then to the left

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: By doing the sunnah acts our Salah is more complete and humble, and we are more present in our conversation with the All-High Lord.

practice.title: Going down to sajdah
practice.prompt: What touches the ground first? Put them in order.
items: The knees
The palms
The face – forehead and nose

questions.q: Must we repeat Salah if we leave out a sunnah act?
How high do men raise their hands at the opening takbir?
When do we raise the right index finger?
Which side do we give the salam to first?
Why should we do the sunnah acts?
options: The Prophet (SAW) did them and they make Salah more complete

practice.title: Questions and tasks
prompts: 💬 What are the sunnah acts of Salah, and what do we gain by doing them?
🤔 Someone leaves out two wajibs and one sunnah, and in the last sitting realises it. What should they do, and why?
💬 Talk with your muallim: “The worst thief is the one who steals from his own Salah.”
